channel.title: Calcitax Advisors News
channel.description: Canadian tax, accounting and finance news in plain language.

item.title: Budget 2026 proposes one May 15 tax deadline for everyone, starting with 2027 returns
item.description: Ottawa wants all individuals, including the self-employed, to file and pay by May 15, starting with 2027 returns. Nothing changes for your 2026 return.

item.title: RDSP grants and bonds: contribute by December 31 to get 2026's government money
item.description: Families with an RDSP can get up to $3,500 in grants and $1,000 in bonds for 2026, but only for contributions made by December 31.

item.title: CCB, CPP and OAS payment dates for November and December 2026
item.description: The last 2026 benefit deposits: CCB and B.C. family benefit on Nov. 20 and Dec. 11, CPP and OAS on Nov. 26 and Dec. 22, and what to do if one is late.

item.title: Canada's unemployment rate rises to 6.7% in October: what it means for you
item.description: Canada's jobless rate rose to 6.7% in October as hiring stalled, while B.C. added 12,000 jobs. What it means for workers, borrowers and small businesses.

item.title: Federal Budget 2026: grocery benefit top-up, refundable caregiver credit and more
item.description: Budget 2026 keeps tax rates the same but proposes a one-time grocery benefit boost, a refundable caregiver credit and an 'RRSP for life'.

item.title: Holiday gifts and parties for staff: how to keep them tax-free in 2026
item.description: Planning gifts or a holiday party for your team? Here are the CRA's $500 gift rule, $150 party limit and gift card conditions, explained.

item.title: Turning 71 in 2026? Your RRSP must be wound up by December 31
item.description: If you turn 71 this year, December 31, 2026 is your last day to contribute to your RRSP and to choose a RRIF, an annuity or cash.

item.title: Paying tax by instalments? Your last 2026 payment is due December 15
item.description: The final 2026 income tax instalment is due Tuesday, December 15. Here's who has to pay, how to check your amount and how to avoid CRA interest.

item.title: Moved from Canada to India this year? Your Canadian tax to-do list
item.description: Leaving Canada for India in 2026? Here's what to file with the CRA: your final return, departure tax forms, and what happens to your accounts and benefits.

item.title: New to Canada in 2026? Your first-year tax and benefits checklist
item.description: Moved to Canada this year? How to apply for benefits now, file your first return by April 30, 2027, and handle property and income from abroad.

item.title: Year-end tax checklist: what to do before December 31, 2026
item.description: Some tax moves only count for 2026 if they happen by December 31. Here's a plain checklist for donations, FHSAs, TFSAs, investment losses and RRSPs.

item.title: 2027 CPP and EI numbers: lower base CPP rate, higher earnings ceilings
item.description: CPP's base rate drops to 4.75% each for workers and employers on January 1, 2027, while the CPP and EI earnings ceilings rise. Here's what changes.

item.title: CRA's new pre-filled tax return: set up your account by October 31
item.description: About one million Canadians will be invited to file a pre-filled 2026 return in March 2027. To qualify, your CRA account must be set up by October 31, 2026.

item.title: Bank of Canada raises its rate to 2.5%: what it means for you
item.description: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate on October 28, 2026, its first increase since 2023, citing higher energy prices and stubborn inflation.

item.title: CRA updates for small businesses: online debt payments, Apple Pay and more
item.description: Business owners can now manage payroll, GST/HST and corporate tax debts online, and pay the CRA with Apple Pay or Google Pay. Here's what's new this fall.
